items.title: The Nature of Discourse (III): Denigration, Right Accord, and Instruction — And Which Are Worth Cultivating

items.zh: 毀謗論者，謂懷憤發者，以染污心振發威勢，更相擯毀所有言論。謂麁惡所引，或不愻所引，或綺言所引；乃至惡說法律中，為諸有情宣說彼法，研究決擇，教授教誡。如是等論，名毀謗論。
items.en: Discourse of denigration: it refers to one who, harbouring resentment, rouses his own force with a defiled mind, the discourse in which each side casts aside and denigrates the other. It is drawn out by coarse and vicious speech, by insolent speech, or by frivolous speech — extending even to expounding, investigating, and teaching a wrongly taught doctrine to others. Discourse of this kind is called discourse of denigration.

items.zh: 順正論者，謂於善說法律中，為諸有情宣說正法，研究決擇，教授教誡。為斷有情所疑惑故，為達甚深諸句義故，為令知見畢竟淨故；隨順正行、隨順解脫，是故此論名順正論。
items.en: Discourse in accord with the right: it refers to expounding, investigating, and teaching the true Dharma to beings within a well-taught doctrine and discipline. It is done to sever beings' doubts, to reach the deep meaning of its statements, and to make knowledge and vision utterly pure — in accord with right practice, in accord with liberation. This is why this discourse is called discourse in accord with the right.

items.zh: 教導論者，謂教修習增上心學、增上慧學補特伽羅，心未定者令心得定，心已定者令得解脫，所有言論。令彼覺悟真實智故，令彼開解真實智故，是故此論名教導論。
items.en: Instructional discourse: it refers to all discourse that teaches a person to cultivate the higher training in mind and the higher training in wisdom — bringing an unconcentrated mind to concentration, and bringing an already-concentrated mind to liberation. It is done to awaken that person to true wisdom and to enable them to open up true wisdom for others; this is why this discourse is called instructional discourse.

items.zh: 問：此六論中，幾論真實，能引義利，所應修習？幾不真實，能引無義，所應遠離？答：最後二論是真是實，能引義利，所應修習；中間二論不真不實，能引無義，所應遠離；初二種論，應當分別。
items.en: Question: among these six kinds of discourse, how many are genuine, capable of bringing real benefit, and worth cultivating? How many are not genuine, bring no real benefit, and should be avoided? Answer: the last two are genuine and real, capable of bringing real benefit, and worth cultivating. The middle two are neither genuine nor real, bring no real benefit, and should be avoided. The first two kinds must be judged case by case.

items.title: The Venue of Discourse: Six Fitting Places to Debate

items.zh: 云何論處所？當知亦有六種。一、於王家，二、於執理家，三、於大眾中，四於賢哲者前，五、於善解法義沙門、婆羅門前，六、於樂法義者前。
items.en: What is the venue of discourse? Know that this too has six kinds: first, at the royal court; second, before a magistrate; third, amid a great assembly; fourth, before the wise and virtuous; fifth, before ascetics and brāhmaṇas well versed in the meaning of the Dharma; and sixth, before those who delight in the meaning of the Dharma.

items.title: The Basis of Discourse Opens: What a Thesis Establishes

items.zh: 云何論所依？當知有十種。謂所成立義有二種，能成立法有八種。所成立義有二種者，一、自性，二、差別。
items.en: What is the basis of discourse? Know that it has ten parts: the meaning to be established has two kinds, and the means of establishing it has eight kinds. The meaning to be established has two kinds: first, self-nature; second, differentiation.

items.zh: 所成立自性者，謂有立為有，無立為無。所成立差別者，謂有上立有上，無上立無上；常立為常，無常立無常。如是有色無色、有見無見、有對無對、有漏無漏、有為無為，如是等無量差別門，當知名所成立差別。
items.en: The self-nature to be established: what has being is posited as being; what has no being is posited as having no being. The differentiation to be established: what is surpassable is posited as surpassable, what is unsurpassed is posited as unsurpassed; what is permanent is posited as permanent, what is impermanent is posited as impermanent. Likewise possessing form or formless, visible or invisible, resistant or non-resistant, defiled or undefiled, conditioned or unconditioned — such immeasurable gateways of differentiation should be known as the differentiation to be established.

items.title: The Eight Means of Establishing a Thesis, and the Three-Part Syllogism Begins

items.zh: 能成立法有八種者，一、立宗，二、辯因，三、引喻，四、同類，五、異類，六、現量，七、比量，八、正教量。
items.en: The means of establishing has eight kinds: first, positing the thesis; second, distinguishing the reason; third, citing the example; fourth, the similar class; fifth, the dissimilar class; sixth, direct perception; seventh, inference; and eighth, valid scriptural authority.

items.zh: 立宗者，謂依二種所成立義，各別攝受自品所許，或攝受論宗。
items.en: Positing the thesis: it means, in dependence on the two kinds of meaning to be established, each distinctly taking up what one's own position accepts — or, being versed in one's own and others' positions, taking up a thesis for discourse.

items.zh: 若自辯才，若輕蔑他，若從他聞，若覺真實。或為成立自宗，或為破壞他宗，或為制伏於他，或為摧屈於他，或為悲愍於他，建立宗義。
辯因者，謂為成就所立宗義，依所引喻、同類、異類現量、比量及與正教，建立順益道理言論。引喻者，亦為成就所立宗義，引因所依諸餘世間串習共許易了之法、比況言論。
items.en: Distinguishing the reason: it means, in order to accomplish the meaning of the thesis posited, establishing discourse that favourably supports it, in dependence on the example cited, the similar class, the dissimilar class, direct perception, inference, and valid scriptural authority. Citing the example: likewise in order to accomplish the meaning of the thesis posited, drawing on some other fact already familiar and mutually agreed upon in the world, on which the reason itself depends, to present discourse by way of comparison.

items.title: The Similar and Dissimilar Class: What Makes an Example Actually Work

items.zh: 同類者，謂隨所有法望所餘法，其相展轉少分相似。此復五種。一、相狀相似，二、自體相似，三、業用相似，四、法門相似，五、因果相似。
items.en: The similar class: it means that, considering any given thing against some other thing, their features turn out, in some small part, to resemble each other. This is again of five kinds: first, resemblance of appearance; second, resemblance of essence; third, resemblance of function; fourth, resemblance of category; and fifth, resemblance of cause and effect.

items.zh: 相狀相似者，謂於現在或先所見相狀相屬展轉相似。自體相似者，謂彼展轉其相相似。業用相似者，謂彼展轉作用相似。法門相似者，謂彼展轉法門相似。如無常與苦法，苦與無我法，無我與生法，生法與老法，老法與死法。如是有色無色、有見無見、有對無對、有漏無漏、有為無為，如是等類無量法門展轉相似。因果相似者，謂彼展轉若因若果、能成所成展轉相似。是名同類。
items.en: Resemblance of appearance: features seen now or seen before turn out, joined together, to resemble each other. Resemblance of essence: their natures turn out, in turn, to resemble each other. Resemblance of function: their activities turn out, in turn, to resemble each other. Resemblance of category: their conceptual domains turn out, in turn, to resemble each other — as with impermanence and suffering, suffering and non-self, non-self and birth, birth and old age, old age and death... and immeasurable domains of this kind that turn out, in turn, to resemble one another. Resemblance of cause and effect: their status as cause and effect, as what accomplishes and what is accomplished, turns out, in turn, to resemble each other. This is called the similar class.

items.zh: 異類者，謂所有法望所餘法，其相展轉少不相似。此亦五種。與上相違，應知其相。
items.en: The dissimilar class: it means that, considering any given thing against some other thing, their features turn out, in some small part, not to resemble each other. This too has five kinds; their character should be known as the reverse of what was said above.

items.title: Direct Perception Opens: Three Conditions for Valid Knowledge

items.zh: 現量者，謂有三種。一、非不現見，二、非已思應思，三、非錯亂境界。
items.en: Direct perception: it has three kinds. First, it is not a case of failing to see directly; second, it is not a matter already deliberated on or yet to be deliberated on; and third, it is not a deceptive object.

blocks.text: Today the treatise says which kinds of discourse are worth engaging in, where debates should take place, and begins the formal method: a thesis, a reason, and an example. Note the teachers' emphasis that the purpose of debate is compassion, not victory.

Denigration "rouses force with a defiled mind". Venerable Miào Jìng: "when his mind stirs, he shows a fearsome look." Discourse **in accord with the right** expounds, investigates, and teaches the true Dharma (Venerable Miào Jìng: hearing, reflection, and cultivation). **Instructional** discourse teaches those already practising (Master Cháng Bǎi: the former is for beginners, the latter for long-time practitioners).

"The last two are genuine and real, worth cultivating. The middle two (contention and denigration) should be avoided. The first two (verbal and worldly) are judged case by case." The treatise does not treat debate as a sport.

Debates should be held before a king, before officials and judges (Venerable Miào Jìng: 執理家 is a judge), in an assembly, before the learned, before Dharma teachers, or before those who seek the Dharma. Venerable Miào Jìng: "Debate isn't just two sides; a third party must be present." Master Cháng Bǎi: the witnesses must be fair.

A thesis establishes either a thing's self-nature (Venerable Miào Jìng: the general statement) or its particulars. "What has being is posited as being; what has none as none." Master Cháng Bǎi reads this through the three natures: the dependent nature is illusory being, the perfected nature real being, the imagined nature non-being.

Eight means establish a thesis: the thesis itself, reason, example, the similar class, the dissimilar class, perception, inference, and scripture. Venerable Miào Jìng: the thesis counts among the means because, as language, it expresses the principle.

Why posit a thesis at all? Master Cháng Bǎi: "the main point in establishing a thesis is compassion for others, helping them turn wrong view into right view." The *Pīxún jì* adds that one must master both one's own position and the opponent's.

A **similar** example resembles the subject "in some small part": Venerable Miào Jìng: sound and a pot are unlike in most ways, but both arise from conditions, so they resemble each other in impermanence. A **dissimilar** example lacks the feature. This is the classic Indian syllogism: "Sound is impermanent (thesis), because it is produced (reason), like a pot (similar example), unlike space (dissimilar example)."
**Perception** (現量) is the first means of valid knowledge. Venerable Miào Jìng: 量 means both a standard and knowing. Three conditions make perception valid; tomorrow's reading explains them.

quiz.q: How does Venerable Miào Jìng map "expounding, investigating, and teaching" in discourse in accord with the right?
options: expounding is hearing-wisdom, investigating reflection-wisdom, instructing cultivation-wisdom
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Expounding the true Dharma is the wisdom of hearing, investigating and deciding the wisdom of reflection, instruction and admonition the wisdom of cultivation." The note's claim that it centres on precepts is not in the lectures.

quiz.q: How do discourse in accord with the right and instructional discourse differ, per Master Cháng Bǎi following Kuījī?
options: the former is for beginners, the latter for long-time practitioners
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "Discourse in accord with the right is for beginning practice; instructional discourse is for long practice — that is the difference." Instruction brings the unconcentrated to concentration and the concentrated to liberation.

quiz.q: Of the six kinds of discourse, which are to be cultivated, avoided, or judged case by case?
options: cultivate the last two; avoid the middle two; judge the first two case by case
quiz.why: "The last two are genuine and real … worth cultivating. The middle two are neither genuine nor real … should be avoided. The first two kinds must be judged case by case." Master Cháng Bǎi: even filial piety, if it involves killing, needs discernment.

quiz.q: What principle, per Master Cháng Bǎi, is common to all six venues of debate?
options: the witnesses must be fair and reasonable so the debate can be fairly judged
it must be in a monastery
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: debate needs a fitting venue, and the witnesses must be fair and rational so that a fair verdict can be reached. Citing Kuījī, the royal court should be one whose king is impartial and respects all religions.

quiz.q: What does Venerable Miào Jìng infer about debate from the six venues?
options: two parties are not enough — a third party must be present
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Debating in these six places shows that debate isn't just two sides — a third party must be there." The first four venues need not understand the Dharma, which is why the fifth specifies it.

quiz.q: The lectures supply the omitted four bases and five purposes of positing a thesis. What is the chief purpose, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: compassion — helping others turn wrong view into right view
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "The main point in establishing a thesis is compassion for others — helping them turn wrong view into right view." Venerable Miào Jìng: the root motive is compassion, with no intent to harm.

quiz.q: The similar class means features resemble "in some small part." What does Venerable Miào Jìng illustrate with sound and a pot?
options: sound and pot are really unlike, but both arise from conditions — they resemble in impermanence
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: sound and a pot, or a drinking cup, are really not alike, but they are all made by conditions — in the sense of impermanence they are alike. Master Cháng Bǎi: the example takes only a partial overlap.
